title: How to Override Pricing Rule for Individual Quotation Items

posts.name: shihab
posts.cooked:
Hi everyone,

We’re trying to implement a custom behavior in ERPNext, where the pricing rule applies by default, but salespersons should be allowed to manually override the rate for individual items in the Quotation and keep that rate without ERPNext forcing the pricing rule again.

Scenario:

Item: ITEM-0001
Default selling price: 140
Pricing Rule applies a 25% discount, so the price becomes 105
During the sales process, the salesperson selects the item and ERPNext correctly applies 105
But when they try to give more discount manually (e.g., change rate to 100), ERPNext resets it back to 105 during save or refresh.

We tried:

Setting “Ignore Pricing Rule”, but that disables all rules for the entire quotation, which we don’t want.
We want to ignore pricing rule per item, not globally.

Our goal is:

Pricing Rule should apply by default.
But if the salesperson manually edits the rate, ERPNext should respect that value and not apply pricing rules again for that item.

How we can achive it, we tried by creating custom app but did’t not succeeded , always erpenxt overiding our custom app logic. or any other method please share.

Has anyone implemented this before? Any guidance or example would be very helpful.

Thanks in advance!

posts.name: shihab
posts.cooked:
After some trial and error, we found a working solution that lets us manually edit item prices in Quotations and other documnets, even when pricing rules are applied.

Goal:

  • Apply pricing rules by default.
  • Allow salesperson to manually override the rate per item.
  • Preserve the manual rate on save/refresh.

Solution:

We monkey-patched ERPNext’s pricing rule logic in a custom app:

import frappe
from frappe.utils import flt
import erpnext.accounts.doctype.pricing_rule.pricing_rule as pricing_rule_module

_original_apply_pricing_rule = pricing_rule_module.apply_pricing_rule
_original_get_pricing_rule_for_item = pricing_rule_module.get_pricing_rule_for_item

def apply_pricing_rule_patch(args, doc=None):
    if getattr(args, "custom_manual_rate", False):
        args.pricing_rule = ""
        args.discount_percentage = 0
        args.margin_type = ""
        args.margin_rate_or_amount = 0
        args.rate = flt(args.rate)
        return
    return _original_apply_pricing_rule(args, doc)

def get_pricing_rule_for_item_patch(args, doc=None, for_validate=False, **kwargs):
    if getattr(args, "custom_manual_rate", False):
        return None
    return _original_get_pricing_rule_for_item(args, doc, for_validate=for_validate, **kwargs)

def override_pricing_rule():
    pricing_rule_module.apply_pricing_rule = apply_pricing_rule_patch
    pricing_rule_module.get_pricing_rule_for_item = get_pricing_rule_for_item_patch

We added a checkbox custom_manual_rate in the Quotation Item table. When the salesperson edits the rate, we tick this checkbox using a simple client script.

This way, ERPNext skips applying pricing rules only for those items.

If there is any other better method please share.

posts.name: Evgheni N.
posts.cooked:
Here is the complete instruction how to create a custom app and implement the solution

bench new-app your_app_name

your_app_name/your_app_name/custom_pricing_rule.py

import copy
import frappe
from frappe.utils import flt
import erpnext.accounts.doctype.pricing_rule.pricing_rule as pricing_rule_module

_original_apply_pricing_rule = pricing_rule_module.apply_pricing_rule
_original_get_pricing_rule_for_item = pricing_rule_module.get_pricing_rule_for_item

def apply_pricing_rule_patch(args, doc=None):
    if getattr(args, "custom_manual_rate", False):
        args.ignore_pricing_rule = 1
        
    return _original_apply_pricing_rule(args, doc)

def get_pricing_rule_for_item_patch(args, doc=None, for_validate=False, **kwargs):
    if getattr(args, "custom_manual_rate", False):
        args.ignore_pricing_rule = 1
        
    return _original_get_pricing_rule_for_item(args, doc, for_validate=for_validate, **kwargs)

your_app_name/your_app_name/init.py

__version__ = "0.0.1"

import frappe
import erpnext.accounts.doctype.pricing_rule.pricing_rule as pricing_rule_module
from your_app_name.custom_pricing_rule import apply_pricing_rule_patch, get_pricing_rule_for_item_patch

pricing_rule_module.apply_pricing_rule = apply_pricing_rule_patch
pricing_rule_module.get_pricing_rule_for_item = get_pricing_rule_for_item_patch

bench restart
bench --site your-site-name.com migrate

posts.name: Sharumathi
posts.cooked:
Hi @shihab0020,

I have a similar requirement, but in the Sales Invoice.

In my case:

  • I have two items in the same Sales Invoice.

  • Both items have applicable Pricing Rules.

  • However, I want to ignore the Pricing Rule for only one specific item and allow the user to manually edit the rate, while the other item should still follow the Pricing Rule normally.

So essentially the behaviour would be:

  • Pricing rules apply by default.

  • If the user manually overrides the rate for a specific row, that row should skip the pricing rule, but other rows should still respect it.

Would the same custom_manual_rate checkbox approach work reliably in the Sales Invoice Item table as well, or is there a more recommended way in ERPNext to selectively bypass pricing rules per item in transactional documents?

Appreciate any suggestions. Thanks!

posts.name: shihab
posts.cooked:
Hi Sharu,

In our experience, trying to override the standard ERPNext pricing rule logic at the individual item level within the core documents led to a lot of complex overrides and maintenance issues.

To achieve this more simply and reliably, we moved away from the standard pricing rule overrides. Instead, we developed a simplified pricing rule system within a custom app. This allows us to have better control over when and how rules are applied without fighting the core logic.

You can check out how we implemented it here: https://github.com/shihab0020/dlitscustom.git
